overall_summary: Bitcoin is seeing clear institutional demand with large corporate buys, whale accumulation, and ETF inflows providing a firm bid. At the same time, rising global yields, a stronger dollar, oil spikes, and renewed US-Iran tensions are feeding risk-off pressure across markets. The tone for crypto is supported underneath but capped by macro and geopolitical headwinds until data and yields clarify direction.
key_points: Heavy BTC buys by Strategy, Strive, and whales
Bond yields surge and dollar firms on hike odds
Oil spikes above $90 on US-Iran clashes
Key US ISM, JOLTS data due today

items.title: Strategy Resumes BTC Buys With $370M Purchase
items.summary: Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, bought 4,603 BTC for about 370 million dollars last week at an average of roughly 80,300 dollars. It was the first purchase in about two months, lifting total holdings to 845,050 BTC. The firm funded it mainly through common stock sales and also did preferred share buybacks. Traders should care because it restarts a major ongoing buyer that has historically supported spot demand and sentiment around corporate treasuries.
items.impact: Adds steady institutional bid and signals renewed corporate confidence

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Rebound With $217M Inflows Led by IBIT
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs flipped back to net inflows of 216.7 million dollars on Monday after Friday's 202 million outflow that ended a nine-day streak. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for about 95 percent of the inflows. Ether ETFs extended their inflow streak to 11 days while XRP and Solana funds also stayed positive. This matters because ETF flows remain a primary driver of spot demand and can quickly reverse or reinforce recent price consolidation near 78,000.
items.impact: Restores institutional flow support after brief outflow pause

items.title: Whales Add 60,000 BTC in August as Retail Sells
items.summary: CryptoQuant data shows wallets holding 100 or more BTC accumulated about 60,000 Bitcoin from August 1 to 30 while smaller holders sold tens of thousands. Whale buying accelerated after the mid-month breakout from the 62 to 65 thousand range. The coins largely stayed off exchanges. Traders should watch this because it indicates strong hands absorbed the rally supply, which can reduce downside pressure if the holdings are not quickly distributed.
items.impact: Improves ownership structure and supports higher support levels

items.title: Strive Buys $143M BTC, Rises to Fifth-Largest Holder
items.summary: Strive purchased 1,800 Bitcoin for approximately 143 million dollars last week at an average near 79,400 dollars, bringing its holdings to 23,156 BTC. That moved it past Bullish into the fifth spot among public corporate holders. Other treasury firms are also adding. This reinforces the trend of listed companies treating Bitcoin as a core balance-sheet asset and provides another source of spot buying pressure alongside Strategy.
items.impact: Broadens corporate demand and validates treasury strategy trend

items.title: Singapore Proposes 100% Reserves and Yield Ban for Stablecoins
items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore opened a consultation on amendments requiring licensed stablecoin issuers to hold full 100 percent reserves in segregated accounts at licensed institutions and banning interest or yield payments to holders. The rules align with US GENIUS Act and EU MiCA approaches and allow limited recognition of some foreign stablecoins. Traders should care because clearer, tighter global stablecoin standards reduce depeg and run risks that can spill into broader crypto liquidity and Bitcoin markets.
items.impact: Supports long-term stability but limits yield products short-term

items.title: Strategy Calls MSCI Proposal Discriminatory to Bitcoin Firms
items.summary: Strategy formally opposed an MSCI consultation that could exclude companies with large non-operating asset holdings, including Bitcoin treasury firms, from global investable indexes. In a letter signed by Michael Saylor and the CEO, the firm called the plan a pretext targeting digital asset treasuries and inconsistent with accounting standards. Index exclusion would matter for passive flows into MSTR and peers, so the outcome could affect correlated Bitcoin exposure vehicles even if direct BTC holdings stay intact.
items.impact: Unresolved index risk for treasury stocks; limited direct BTC effect yet

items.title: Global Bond Selloff Intensifies as Yields Hit Multi-Year Highs
items.summary: US 10-year Treasury yields climbed to around 4.78 to 4.79 percent, their highest since early 2025, while Japan's 10-year yield touched 3 percent for the first time since 1996 and European yields also surged. The move stems from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks plus rising oil prices from renewed Middle East fighting. Traders should care because higher yields raise discount rates, pressure equities and crypto, and signal tighter financial conditions heading into the September FOMC.
items.impact: Higher yields and tighter conditions weigh on risk assets including Bitcoin

items.title: Markets Now Price 65 Percent Chance of September Fed Hike
items.summary: Following Warsh's Jackson Hole speech stressing the need to get inflation back to 2 percent and that current policy is not very restrictive, futures markets have lifted the probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the mid-September FOMC to about 65 percent. Core PCE remains elevated near 3.3 percent. This shifts the rate path higher and supports the dollar while challenging leveraged and growth-sensitive assets.
items.impact: Increased hike odds tighten liquidity expectations and pressure crypto

items.title: Eurozone Inflation Jumps to 3.3 Percent on Energy Surge
items.summary: Preliminary August Eurozone HICP inflation rose to 3.3 percent year-over-year from 2.9 percent in July, matching forecasts, with energy inflation spiking to 14.3 percent amid Middle East tensions. Core inflation eased slightly to 2.4 percent. The print locks in market expectations for an ECB rate hike next week and adds to the global inflation and bond-yield pressure.
items.impact: Supports further central-bank tightening and higher global yields

items.title: Oil Tops 90 Dollars as US-Iran Clashes Reignite Inflation Fears
items.summary: Brent crude pushed above 91 to 92 dollars a barrel after renewed military exchanges between the US and Iran, the first major escalation in weeks. Higher energy costs feed directly into inflation readings and reinforce the case for central banks to stay hawkish or hike. Crypto traders watch this because sticky inflation delays any pivot to easier policy.
items.impact: Inflation impulse strengthens hawkish policy pricing and risk-off flows

items.title: US Dollar Firms as Yields Rise and Safe-Haven Demand Builds
items.summary: The DXY dollar index climbed toward 99.6, gaining on higher Treasury yields, elevated Fed hike odds, and geopolitical safe-haven flows. A stronger dollar typically acts as a headwind for Bitcoin and other risk assets priced in dollars. Watch for further upside if today's US data or Barr comments reinforce the hawkish narrative.
items.impact: Stronger dollar pressures crypto and emerging-market risk assets

items.title: Key US Data Today: ISM Manufacturing, JOLTS and Construction
items.summary: Markets await the August ISM Manufacturing PMI, expected near 55.2 after 55.6, July JOLTS job openings forecast around 7.3 million, and July construction spending. These land ahead of Friday's nonfarm payrolls and feed into September FOMC pricing. Soft prints could temper hike bets while strong ones, especially on prices or openings, would reinforce the hawkish shift. Fed Governor Barr is also due to speak.
items.impact: Data will drive near-term rate-path and risk-asset volatility into NFP

items.title: US-Iran Strikes Resume; Hormuz Tankers Hit, Oil Spikes
items.summary: After a month of relative calm, the US struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz to stop mine-laying, and Iran fired back at US bases in Jordan. Trump vowed to hit Iran hard, while reports came in of tankers struck by projectiles in the strait. Brent crude climbed back above 91 dollars a barrel on supply fears. Traders should care because this keeps energy prices elevated, feeds inflation worries, and keeps risk assets under pressure as the six-month war shows no quick end.
items.impact: Higher oil and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: White House Details Historic Venezuela Oil Control Deal
items.summary: The Trump administration released a fact sheet on its deal giving the US majority influence over more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan reserves through a private partner, North American Blue Energy Partners. The US gets a 35 percent equity stake via the Pentagon, rights to buy 20 percent of output at cost for the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, and board veto power. Trump said the US will take all of that oil. This matters for traders as it signals potential long-term boost to Western Hemisphere supply that could eventually ease oil prices and energy inflation.
items.impact: Potential medium-term oil supply increase supporting risk assets

items.title: Trump Brings Russia Back to G20; Europe Snubs Photo
items.summary: Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attended the US-hosted G20 finance ministers meeting in Asheville for the first time in person since the Ukraine invasion, meeting Treasury Secretary Bessent. European officials refused the traditional family photo with him and voiced strong objections. Trump defended it saying he likes getting along with everybody, while Bessent stressed no economic relief until the war ends. Crypto traders should watch this as a signal of shifting US-Russia diplomacy that could affect sanctions, energy markets, and broader geopolitical risk premiums.
items.impact: Diplomatic thaw signal but Europe friction keeps uncertainty high

items.title: Russia's Sixth Night of Strikes Kills Dozen in Kyiv Area
items.summary: Russian missiles and drones pounded Kyiv and surrounding areas overnight, killing at least 12 people including railway workers and injuring others, with fires across multiple districts. It marked the sixth straight night of attacks on the capital as Ukraine struggles with air defense shortages. Zelenskyy called for more interceptors from allies. This keeps the Ukraine war hot and could pressure European energy and defense spending, feeding into broader risk sentiment for markets.
items.impact: Sustained European security risk and potential energy volatility

items.title: Xi, Putin, Modi Deepen Ties at SCO Summit in Bishkek
items.summary: Leaders including China's Xi Jinping, Russia's Putin, India's Modi, and Iran's president gathered in Kyrgyzstan for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit marking 25 years. Xi and Putin pledged deeper coordination amid global uncertainty, framing the group as a multipolar counterweight. The meeting comes as both Russia and Iran face Western pressure from ongoing wars. Traders note this as a potential strengthening of non-Western economic and energy alignments that could influence sanctions evasion and commodity flows.
items.impact: Longer-term multipolar shift with mixed effects on sanctions and trade

items.title: US Army Secretary Resigns Amid Hegseth Tensions, Two Wars
items.summary: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation after clashing with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over leadership firings and transformation efforts. The Army now lacks confirmed top civilian and military leaders while engaged in the Iran conflict and supporting Ukraine. The White House praised his work but the exit adds to a string of Pentagon shakeups. Markets watch military leadership stability as a signal of US capacity to manage simultaneous conflicts without further escalation or readiness gaps.
items.impact: Political-military uncertainty with limited immediate price catalyst
